biggest_gap.title: The health-check fault is not fixed: verify's health check still fails ours with a false 'action outside the clock', now on add-rate, and the new posted-task rule gives the reason
biggest_gap.detail:
This round's one job was to stop the harness's built-ours health check from blaming a harness DevTools command for a page change a step made. In my clean-clone alone verify the e2e stage failed on exactly that, on a quiet machine (load about 1). The product did what the step asked (the rate was saved, screenshot 03).

What the verdict says: add-rate INVALID, 'the page changed what it shows without a counted step causing it (1 change; 0.465 s into the measured part, a StyleRecalcInvalidationTracking: a task posted by a task no step caused: a DevTools command outside any step (the harness reading the page))'. Step 4, Enter to save, ran at 0.454 s.

Where it comes from: the new postedCause in lib/causation.mjs links a task to its poster through Chromium's flow ids. Here the poster was a harness read, which pointCause judges 'no step'. So a follow-up task that interleaves with the harness's own read now inherits 'not caused', even when the change belongs to the step around it.

It is intermittent: 1 time in 4 clean-stack runs (my verify invalid; health runs 1 to 3 on a fresh stack verified add-rate).

Suspected fix: a task posted during a DevTools command that only reads, while a step's input is being handled, should be judged by the step's input. Alternatively, when the poster is a harness read, fall back to the pre-round-15 judgement instead of declaring the change uncaused. Add a real-browser control in which the harness reads the page between a key and the change.
